title: Thyroid Hormone: Tissues Decide What T4 Becomes

generated.pipeline: extract → Opus draft → Sonnet accuracy gate → Sonnet fixes

cards.front: A person with no thyroid takes only T4, yet has T3 in the blood. Where does the T3 come from?
cards.back: From the rest of the body: tissues remove one iodine atom from T4 to make T3.
cards.why: So tissues, as well as the gland, decide how much active hormone each cell gets.
cards.quote: The thyroid secretes mostly T4, and tissues remove one iodine atom to make T3, so tissues, as well as the gland, decide how much active hormone each cell gets.

cards.front: Name the four stations of the thyroid hormone loop and what happens at each.
cards.back: Make (the gland, mostly T4); carry (blood, almost all protein-bound); convert (each tissue switches T4 on to T3 or off); sense (the pituitary sets TSH).
cards.quote: Thyroid hormone runs around one loop with four stations. The gland makes it, mostly as T4.

cards.front: With the thyroid loop intact and at steady state, do binding proteins change total or free hormone?
cards.back: Total (the stored, bound hormone). The loop holds the free hormone steady.
cards.quote: Binding proteins change how much hormone is stored (the total), not how much is free (unbound)

cards.front: A person with no thyroid takes a fixed daily dose of T4. What sets their free T4, and why can TSH not correct it?
cards.back: The absorbed dose and clearance. The loop is open: there is no gland for TSH to drive.
cards.quote: free T4 is set by the absorbed dose and clearance, not by TSH.

cards.front: Why is T3, not T4, treated as the active thyroid hormone?
cards.back: T3 binds the thyroid hormone receptor much more tightly than T4. T4 is best treated as a prohormone that tissues can switch on.
cards.quote: T3 binds the thyroid hormone receptor much more tightly than T4 does, so T3 is the form that acts.
cards.section: The gland sends mostly T4; tissues decide how much becomes T3

cards.front: In human blood, roughly what fraction of T4 and of T3 is free?
cards.back: T4: about 3 molecules in 10,000 (99.97 percent bound). T3: about 3 in 1,000 (99.70 percent bound).
cards.quote: In human blood about 99.97 percent of T4 is bound, so only about 3 molecules in 10,000 are free.
cards.section: Carry: almost all of it rides on proteins

cards.front: Which pool of plasma thyroid hormone do transporters carry into cells and the pituitary sense: bound or free?
cards.back: The free (unbound) fraction. The bound hormone is a store.
cards.quote: The free fraction, the unbound part, is what transporters carry into cells and what the pituitary senses.
cards.section: Carry: almost all of it rides on proteins

cards.front: Assume the cells that clear thyroid hormone take up only free molecules, and T4 is about ten times less free than T3. Which has the longer plasma half-life, and what follows for a once-daily T4 tablet?
cards.back: T4: about 6.2 days against about 1 day for T3 in euthyroid people. Most T4 is parked on carriers, so clearing cells reach it slowly; the long half-life gives steady levels on one tablet a day.
cards.why: Binding is one reason for the difference, not the only one.
cards.quote: In people with normal thyroid function (euthyroid), the half-life of T4 is about 6.2 days, against about 1 day for T3.
cards.section: Carry: almost all of it rides on proteins

cards.front: Which deiodinases switch T4 on to T3, and from which ring do they remove an iodine?
cards.back: D1 and D2, from the outer ring.
cards.quote: D1 and D2 remove an iodine from the outer ring and make T3.
cards.section: Convert: which ring loses an iodine decides on or off

cards.front: D3 removes an inner-ring iodine. What does it make from T4, and from T3?
cards.back: From T4, reverse T3 (inactive); from T3, 3,3'-T2. D3 switches the hormone off.
cards.quote: It turns T4 into reverse T3, which is inactive, and T3 into 3,3'-diiodothyronine (3,3'-T2).
cards.section: Convert: which ring loses an iodine decides on or off

cards.front: How can a tissue set its own T3 supply without any change in plasma T3?
cards.back: D2 often works inside the very cell that will use the T3, converting free T4 locally; D3 can switch hormone off in the same tissue.
cards.quote: D2 often works inside the very cell that will use the T3.
cards.section: Convert: which ring loses an iodine decides on or off

cards.front: One tissue raises its D3 and lowers its D2 while plasma T4 and T3 stay normal. What happens to the T3 reaching that tissue's nuclei, and would a blood test show it?
cards.back: It falls: less T4 is switched on, and more T4 and T3 are switched off. A blood test may miss it, because one tissue's change is small against the whole body's supply.
cards.quote: Less T4 is switched on inside those cells, and more of both T4 and T3 is switched off.
cards.section: Convert: which ring loses an iodine decides on or off

cards.front: An infant boy has global developmental delay, a high serum T3, a low-normal T4 and a mildly raised TSH. Which station of the thyroid loop has failed, and why does the blood not reflect his brain?
cards.back: Entry into cells: a defect in the transporter MCT8 (an X-linked gene). The blood has plenty of T3, but the developing brain cannot take it in.
cards.why: Blood tests report the supply, not the tissue.
cards.quote: yet the developing brain, which depends on MCT8 to take the hormone in, behaves as if starved of it.
cards.section: Getting in: transporters

cards.front: Radiolabelled T4 was given to patients who were athyreotic or hypothyroid and taking T4, and labelled T3 appeared in their serum. What does this show?
cards.back: T4 is converted to T3 outside the thyroid, in humans. It did not identify the enzyme or organ, or measure how much T3 is made this way.
cards.quote: The result ruled in conversion outside the thyroid, in humans.
cards.section: The evidence: T3 is made outside the gland

cards.front: In the athyreotic labelled-T4 study, two controls were added: a purified label with under 0.1 percent T3, and T4 given into a vein. Which dull explanation does each rule out?
cards.back: The purified label rules out injected contaminating T3. Intravenous T4 rules out conversion confined to the gut during absorption.
cards.quote: A specially purified lot of labelled T4, with less than 0.1 percent contaminating T3, gave the same result, so the T3 had not simply been injected.
cards.section: The evidence: T3 is made outside the gland

cards.front: In humans, what does too little thyroid hormone around birth impair, and what public health measure follows?
cards.back: Growth of the skeleton and the brain. Many countries screen newborns for congenital hypothyroidism.
cards.quote: In humans, too little around birth impairs growth of the skeleton and the brain, and many countries screen newborns for congenital hypothyroidism.
cards.section: What T3 does: development first, then heat and the heart

cards.front: Why do the main effects of T3 build over hours to days rather than seconds?
cards.back: T3 acts mainly through thyroid hormone receptors, nuclear receptors that regulate transcription.
cards.quote: T3 acts mainly through thyroid hormone receptors, nuclear receptors that regulate transcription, so its main effects build over hours to days.
cards.section: What T3 does: development first, then heat and the heart

cards.front: By what two routes is thyroid hormone thought to raise heat production?
cards.back: Making less ATP per fuel burned (mitochondrial uncoupling), and ATP-using processes that turn ATP into heat: the sodium-potassium pump, SERCA calcium cycling with sarcolipin, futile substrate cycles. Which matters most is still argued.
cards.quote: Part of the extra heat is thought to come from making less ATP per fuel burned
cards.section: What T3 does: development first, then heat and the heart

cards.front: What does thyroid hormone do to heart rate, contractile force, systemic vascular resistance and cardiac output?
cards.back: Raises heart rate and contractile force, lowers SVR, so cardiac output rises.
cards.quote: Thyroid hormone raises heart rate and contractile force and lowers systemic vascular resistance (SVR)
cards.section: What T3 does: development first, then heat and the heart

cards.front: In a made-up thyrotoxic patient, cardiac output rises to 1.5 times normal and systemic vascular resistance falls to two-thirds of normal. Using mean arterial pressure ≈ cardiac output × SVR, what happens to mean arterial pressure?
cards.back: MAP ratio = 1.5 × (2/3) = 1.0, so mean pressure is unchanged.
cards.why: Lower SVR offsets the higher cardiac output, so mean pressure may change little.
cards.quote: Since mean arterial pressure is roughly cardiac output times SVR, mean pressure may change little.
cards.section: What T3 does: development first, then heat and the heart

cards.front: Which hypothalamic hormone drives TSH release, and through what kind of receptor does TSH act on follicular cells?
cards.back: TRH, reaching the anterior pituitary through portal vessels; TSH acts through a G protein-coupled receptor.
cards.quote: TSH acts through a G protein-coupled receptor on follicular cells (G proteins) to raise synthesis and release
cards.section: Sense: one loop holds free hormone steady

cards.front: T3 is the feedback signal, yet TSH tracks free T4 closely. Why?
cards.back: Much of the T3 acting in the pituitary is thought to be made there from T4 by D2, so the pituitary reads free T4 as well as free T3.
cards.quote: Much of the T3 acting in the pituitary is thought to be made there from T4 by D2
cards.section: Sense: one loop holds free hormone steady

cards.front: Why is TSH usually the most sensitive single readout of a problem in the thyroid gland itself?
cards.back: TSH changes steeply with small changes in free hormone.
cards.quote: TSH changes steeply with small changes in free hormone, so it is usually the most sensitive single readout
cards.section: Sense: one loop holds free hormone steady

cards.front: In a made-up adult, total plasma T4 is 80 nmol per L and 99.97 percent is protein-bound. What is free T4, in pmol per L?
cards.back: Free fraction = 1 − 0.9997 = 0.0003. Free T4 = 80 × 0.0003 = 0.024 nmol per L = 24 pmol per L.
cards.quote: 80 nmol per L × 0.0003 = 0.024 nmol per L = 24 pmol per L.
cards.section: Worked problem: a rise in binding protein

cards.front: In a made-up adult at steady state, total T4 is 120 nmol per L, with TBG carrying 75 percent and other carriers 25 percent. TBG rises to 1.5 times its old value; feedback is intact and affinities are unchanged. What are the new total T4 and free T4?
cards.back: Free T4 returns to its old value, so bound T4 scales with each carrier. TBG part: 0.75 × 120 = 90, × 1.5 = 135. Others: 0.25 × 120 = 30. Total = 165 nmol per L (1.375 times); free T4 unchanged.
cards.quote: With free T4 back at 24 pmol per L, each carrier is as saturated as before, so bound hormone scales with carrier concentration.
cards.section: Worked problem: a rise in binding protein

cards.front: After estrogen raises TBG in a person with an intact thyroid loop, free T4 dips and then returns to normal. What brings it back?
cards.back: The dip raises TSH, which pushes gland output up until free T4 is back where the pituitary holds it. The extra hormone parks on the new TBG.
cards.why: At steady state the gland's output must again match the clearance of free hormone.
cards.quote: TSH keeps pushing output up until free T4 is back where the pituitary holds it.
cards.section: Worked problem: a rise in binding protein

cards.front: Estrogen raises TBG. Predict total T4, free T4 and TSH in a woman with normal thyroid function, and in a woman with hypothyroidism on a fixed dose of T4.
cards.back: Normal function: total T4 rises, free T4 and TSH unchanged. Fixed T4 dose: total T4 rises, free T4 falls and TSH rises, because TSH cannot raise a fixed supply.
cards.why: Rests on the rule that the loop, not binding chemistry alone, defends the free level; an open loop cannot.
cards.quote: In women with hypothyroidism taking T4, total T4 and TBG rose in the same way, but free T4 fell and TSH rose
cards.section: Estrogen with an open loop

cards.front: A person with no thyroid changes their fixed daily T4 dose. Taking the T4 half-life as 6.2 days (one pool, first-order elimination), how far toward the new steady level is T4 after 18.6 days?
cards.back: 18.6 / 6.2 = 3 half-lives. Fraction = 1 − 2^(−3) = 1 − 0.125 = 0.875, so 87.5 percent of the way. T4 changes take about a month to settle.
cards.quote: Each half-life closes half the remaining gap, so after n half-lives T4 is 1 − 2^(−n) of the way to its new steady level
cards.section: Back to the opening patient: an open loop

cards.front: What fills the lumen of a thyroid follicle?
cards.back: Colloid, a protein gel made mostly of thyroglobulin.
cards.quote: a lumen of colloid, a protein gel made mostly of thyroglobulin
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: How does the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS) move iodide into a follicular cell against its gradient, and on which face?
cards.back: Secondary active transport on the basolateral (blood) face: the inward sodium gradient, kept by the sodium-potassium pump, drives iodide in.
cards.quote: moves iodide into the cell against its gradient, driven by the inward sodium gradient that the sodium-potassium pump maintains
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: A drug blocks the sodium-potassium pump in thyroid follicular cells. What happens to iodide trapping by NIS, and why?
cards.back: It falls. The inward sodium gradient runs down, and NIS needs that gradient to move iodide in, two sodium ions with each iodide.
cards.why: NIS is secondary active transport; it uses the sodium gradient, not ATP directly.
cards.quote: two sodium ions move in with each iodide, one net positive charge per cycle
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: At the apical surface of a follicular cell, what do thyroperoxidase (TPO) and dual oxidase (DUOX) each do?
cards.back: DUOX supplies hydrogen peroxide; TPO uses it to oxidize iodide and attach it to thyroglobulin tyrosines, making MIT and DIT (organification).
cards.quote: thyroperoxidase (TPO) uses hydrogen peroxide from dual oxidase (DUOX) to oxidize iodide and attach it to tyrosines of thyroglobulin
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: On thyroglobulin, DIT plus DIT gives T4; {{c1::MIT}} plus DIT gives T3.
cards.quote: DIT plus DIT gives T4; MIT plus DIT gives T3.
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: List the steps by which stored T4 and T3 leave the thyroid follicle under TSH stimulation.
cards.back: Endocytosis of colloid, fusion of vesicles with lysosomes, protease digestion of thyroglobulin, exit through basolateral transporters such as MCT8.
cards.quote: the cell takes colloid back in by endocytosis, the vesicles fuse with lysosomes, proteases digest thyroglobulin
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: A drug blocks thyroperoxidase in a person with an intact thyroid loop. Predict free T4, TSH and gland size over the following weeks.
cards.back: Organification and hormone synthesis fall, so free T4 falls; less T3 inhibits TRH and TSH release, so TSH rises; sustained TSH enlarges the gland over weeks.
cards.why: Combines the make station (TPO organifies iodide) with the sense station (T3 feedback; TSH enlarges the gland).
cards.quote: T3 inhibits TRH and TSH release.
cards.section: Sense: one loop holds free hormone steady

cards.front: In compensated iodine deficiency, predict TSH, free T4, T3 and radioiodine uptake.
cards.back: TSH normal or high; free T4 normal or low; T3 normal or high (preserved); uptake high, because little stable iodide competes with the tracer.
cards.quote: Iodine is the raw material, so when it is short, it limits the hormone supply
cards.section: Make: how the follicle builds hormone, and what the scan sees

cards.front: An adult has a low free T4 and a TSH in the normal range. Where is the fault most likely, and why?
cards.back: At the pituitary or hypothalamus (secondary hypothyroidism). A working pituitary would raise TSH against a low free T4; a TSH not that high means a broken sensor.
cards.quote: a TSH not as high as a low free T4 demands suggests a problem at the pituitary or hypothalamus
cards.section: Locating a fault: read the pair, then the scan

cards.front: In untreated primary hypothyroidism, what are TSH, free T4 and T3?
cards.back: TSH high, free T4 low; T3 can stay normal and may fall when severe.
cards.quote: Can stay normal; may fall when severe
cards.section: Locating a fault: read the pair, then the scan

cards.front: Radioiodine uptake measures what fraction of a tracer dose the thyroid holds hours later. Which processes determine it?
cards.back: Trapping by NIS, organification, the stable iodide supply and tracer loss.
cards.quote: which depends on trapping by NIS, organification, the stable iodide supply and tracer loss
cards.section: The radioiodine scan asks what the gland is doing

cards.front: Graves disease and early thyroiditis both give a high free T4 and a suppressed TSH. Which shows high radioiodine uptake, and why does the other not?
cards.back: Graves disease usually shows high uptake: antibodies drive the gland to make new hormone from new iodide, so it traps tracer. In thyroiditis damaged follicles trap little iodide; the excess is stored hormone leaking out.
cards.quote: Graves disease, whose gland is making new hormone from new iodide and so traps tracer.
cards.section: Same blood, different scan: Graves disease and thyroiditis

cards.front: An adult has a suppressed TSH, a high free T4 and low radioiodine uptake, with no recent iodine load. Besides early thyroiditis, what explanation must be excluded, and why does it give the same pattern?
cards.back: Thyroid hormone taken as a drug (or made outside the gland). Excess hormone suppresses TSH, so the unstimulated gland traps little tracer.
cards.why: Low uptake is not specific to thyroiditis; the scan is read with the hormone pattern, never alone.
cards.quote: Low uptake is not specific to it: thyroid hormone taken as a drug, and hormone made outside the gland, do the same.
cards.section: The radioiodine scan asks what the gland is doing

cards.front: Predict metabolic rate, heart rate, cardiac output and systemic vascular resistance in untreated Graves disease, and name the rule each prediction rests on.
cards.back: Metabolic rate and heat up, heart faster, cardiac output higher, SVR lower. Thyrotoxicosis exaggerates the normal actions of T3, and antibody stimulation of the TSH receptor continues despite suppressed TSH.
cards.quote: thyrotoxicosis (excess thyroid hormone) exaggerates the actions of T3 above: higher metabolic rate and heat, faster heart, higher cardiac output, lower SVR
cards.section: Same blood, different scan: Graves disease and thyroiditis

cards.front: Mice lacking type 2 deiodinase (D2) became hypothermic in the cold because brown fat thermogenesis failed, yet plasma T3 was normal; one T3 injection reversed the brown fat abnormalities. What does this show, and name one key control.
cards.back: Brown fat relies on T3 made inside its own cells from T4 by D2; plasma T3 does not fully report its thyroid status. Controls: e.g. confirm normal sympathetic drive to brown fat, or wild-type littermates in the same cold.
cards.why: The T3 rescue points to missing tissue T3 rather than some other D2 function.
cards.quote: Plasma T3 was normal, yet the tissue behaved as if it lacked thyroid hormone.
cards.section: Design problem

cards.front: In human muscle after three days of T3, NMR estimated that TCA cycle flux rose by about 70 percent while ATP synthesis did not increase. What does this imply about ATP made per turn of the cycle, and what mechanism?
cards.back: ATP per turn fell to about 1.0 / 1.7 = 0.59 of baseline. The authors read this as mitochondrial uncoupling: more fuel oxidized per ATP, the difference released as heat.
cards.why: Fluxes are model-based estimates in seven people over three days.
cards.quote: Instead TCA flux rose by about 70 percent while estimated ATP synthesis did not increase.
cards.section: How T3 becomes heat: the muscle NMR study
